description:
## Goal

Make PR #110 the semantic-correctness foundation and PR #118 the recalculator layer in one GitHub stack:

```text
main
  -> PR #110 wt/kdt-close
       -> PR #118 fz-tfn/long-lived-recalculator
```

Replay every delivered PR #118 ticket commit onto PR #110 in original order, reconcile each semantic conflict to one surviving authority, and establish a proven combined baseline before any other unfinished epic child proceeds.

This is integration work, not a mechanical history rewrite. Correct semantic identity must precede persistent reuse.

## Ground truth

At evaluation time:

- both branches fork from exact base `a3a9761d1`;
- PR #110 head is `f986da97e`, fourteen unique commits, +10,185/-1,531 across 70 files;
- PR #118 delivered head is `5b1007463`, fourteen unique commits, +12,903/-6,176 across 71 files, with `fz-tfn.9` still required before this ticket starts;
- 27 files overlap;
- merge-tree reports conflicts in `.agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md`, `.agent/docs/fact-engine.md`, `src/compiler2/canon.rs`, `src/compiler2/drive.rs`, `src/compiler2/drive_test.rs`, `src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs`, `src/compiler2/types/canon.rs`, and `src/telemetry/public_trace_test.rs`;
- both PRs are draft and green; neither is currently registered as a GitHub stack;
- PR #110 fixes semantic meaning, activation keying, brands, dispatch selection, and input-dependent returns; PR #118 owns sharing, persistence, exact causality, and edge-triggered recalculation.

No open epic child is fully completed by PR #110. Its new semantics change the baselines and assumptions of `fz-tfn.1`, `.6`, `.9`, `.13`, `.14`, `.18`, `.19`, `fz-kdt.4`, `.48`, `.57`, `.58`, `.165`, `.169`, and `.182`.

## Required combined model

- World owns authoritative interned semantic facts.
- Each retained root ProductMemo is the sole product authority and stores shared immutable answers.
- One dependency index ignites work from exact fact/product movement; no root, activation, waiter, or inventory scan is restored.
- Monotone cycles converge through ordinary per-key reactive formulas, not private cone/fixpoint solvers.
- Types owns one-denotation/one-Ty identity and one operation-tagged memoized comparison authority. Rendered or canonical strings remain display/debug output only.
- Callable resolution has one dependency-tracked authority.
- Native reuse is ultimately keyed by stable semantic body/content rather than whole-root remapping.

## Strategy

1. Start only after `fz-tfn.9` is committed, closed, pushed, and fully green remotely.
2. Record exact heads, verify all involved worktrees clean, and create immutable backup refs for both PR heads.
3. Initialize the local GitHub stack with #110 below #118, then rebase #118 onto #110 without rebasing #110 onto main.
4. Replay PR #118 commits in original ticket order. Resolve a conflict inside the historical ticket commit only when the resolution is already within that ticket description. Never close a ticket again.
5. Preserve `fz-tfn.5` deletion of the standing root-entry scan. Translate PR #110 InputDemand gating into exact surviving dependencies; do not resurrect scanner authority.
6. Fold PR #110 construction-member seat/drop behavior into the dependency-tracked CallableResolution path; do not retain two edge constructors.
7. Route PR #110 production type ordering through typed memoized operations; do not retain canonical/display-string or raw interner-order authority.
8. Combine brand refinement with binder-scoped typed canonical structure.
9. Recompute causal and population ratchets from the combined implementation. Never select either parent branch constants by convenience.
10. If a necessary reconciliation is not honestly owned by an existing ticket description, put it in this ticket single integration commit when it is purely a branch-composition invariant. If it is a separable semantic or architectural feature, create a new child ticket, make it a dependency, and do not smuggle it into rebased history.
11. Fresh cold-review every rewritten commit against its new parent. Give special scrutiny to `fz-kdt.47`, `fz-tfn.5`, `fz-kdt.163`, `fz-tfn.26`, `fz-kdt.5`, `fz-tfn.4`, and `fz-tfn.9`.
12. Add exactly one commit for this ticket containing any required combined-model reconciliation, documentation, mapping/proof record, and final ratchet updates not owned by prior tickets.
13. Submit the GitHub stack, preserve both PRs as draft, and verify #118 targets `wt/kdt-close` with stack order #110 -> #118.

## Required ticket/DAG re-evaluation

Before closing, rewrite affected open ticket descriptions to the combined ground truth, without contradictory comments. In particular:

- create or refine one reactive InputDemand ticket that deletes `derive_input_demand` / `solve_forwarded_demand` private cone work and expresses local, forwarded, returned-key, and later callable-identity demand as ordinary exact-dependency formulas;
- evaluate `fz-kdt.214` as the shared correctness prerequisite for direct, reconstructed, and projected forwarding edges before `fz-kdt.165`;
- evaluate whether `fz-kdt.213` folds into reactive InputDemand or blocks native incrementality/final acceptance;
- redefine `fz-kdt.165` as an additional dimension of the existing InputDemand fact, not another fact or cone;
- ensure `fz-tfn.13` can absorb and ultimately delete `fz-kdt.163` post-lowering whole-root remap/equivalence work;
- preserve `fz-tfn.10` through `.12` deletion of PullSession/World mirrors and reassess nested shared handles afterward;
- record a separate harness ticket if one corpus compilation can feed multiple permanent ratchets without weakening non-vacuity or failure attribution.

## Acceptance

- Backup refs name the exact pre-rebase PR heads and are pushed or otherwise durable before force-updating shared branches.
- #110 remains a clean, independently reviewable lower PR against main.
- #118 contains all delivered ticket changes, in original logical order, on top of #110 and shows only the recalculator layer in its PR diff.
- Every textual and semantic conflict has an explicit owner and one surviving authority; no both-path compatibility shim remains.
- No root-entry scan, duplicate callable-resolution constructor, display-string comparison authority, or invented causal exception is introduced.
- `fz-tfn.9` clone/identity measurements are repeated on the combined population; temporary probes leave before commit.
- Exact structured causal reports are regenerated for all five request scenarios across 00420, predicate, and range fixtures and are cross-process identical with zero exclusions.
- Full library, CLI, all target doors, serial fixture matrix, formatting, diff checks, and strict all-target/all-feature clippy pass without controlled warnings.
- Each rewritten ticket commit receives fresh ticket-scoped cold approval; the integration commit receives its own cold review.
- A mapping from every old PR #118 commit hash to its rebased hash and verification evidence is recorded in an agent-facing measurement/proof document.
- Both PRs remain draft, CI is fully green for the submitted stack, and no unfinished epic child remains unblocked by this ticket.
- Temporary worktrees, conflict backups, probes, switches, and reconciliation scaffolding are removed after durable recovery refs and proof exist.
title: Stack recalculator work on semantic-correctness PR #110
